title: The lost key
intro: It is eight in the morning, Mina has to go to work – and her key has vanished. She looks everywhere in the flat. The story practises the words for places in a home, the prepositions روی 'on', زیر 'under' and در 'in', and the negative نیست 'is not'. Her daughter Sara solves the mystery with a sentence that plays with one little Persian word.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.en: It is eight o'clock in the morning.

sentences.fa: مینا می‌خواهد به سر کار برود.
sentences.r: Minā mi-khāhad be sar-e kār be-ravad.
sentences.en: Mina wants to go to work.
The key is not in her bag.
It is not on the table.
It is not under the carpet either.
The key is not in the fridge!
Mina asks: "Sara, where is my key?"

sentences.fa: سارا به در خانه نگاه می‌کند و می‌خندد.
sentences.r: Sārā be dar-e khāne negāh mi-konad o mi-khandad.
sentences.en: Sara looks at the front door and laughs.

sentences.fa: او می‌گوید: «مامان، کلید در در است!»
sentences.r: u mi-guyad: «māmān, kelid dar dar ast!»
sentences.en: She says: "Mum, the key is in the door!"

sentences.fa: کلید از دیشب در قفل در است.
sentences.r: kelid az dishab dar ghofl-e dar ast.
sentences.en: The key has been in the lock since last night.

sentences.fa: مینا می‌خندد و کلید را برمی‌دارد.
sentences.r: Minā mi-khandad o kelid rā bar-mi-dārad.
sentences.en: Mina laughs and takes the key.

questions.q: What time is it at the start of the story?
Where does Mina want to go?

options: in the lock of the door

after: Sara's sentence کلید در در است is a little joke on the word در, which means both 'door' and 'in' – written the same and both pronounced dar. So the sentence is literally 'key in door is'. In the third paragraph you see how Persian says 'not either': زیر فرش هم نیست 'it isn't under the carpet either' – هم 'too' works in negative sentences as well. And notice کجاست 'where is it?': in writing, است often joins the word before it after a vowel, کجا + است → کجاست.
